name: Passkey MFA to Home
summary: A password-proved user with a pending MFA challenge completes a valid user-verified Passkey assertion for the challenge-bound account, consumes the MFA challenge, and receives the authenticated application session.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and a password-issued MFA challenge is active for an existing durable identity and provider passkey is included in the challenge's allowed providers

serverInteraction.intent: Validate the password-issued MFA challenge for provider passkey, use its UserId to issue and validate a user-bound Passkey assertion requiring user verification, advance the signature counter, consume the MFA challenge only after successful Passkey proof, and establish the platform-appropriate application session.

postconditions.expression: credential-proof == passkey-proved, the password-issued MFA challenge is consumed, and session-capability in [authenticated-limited,authenticated-normal]

sourceReferences.note: The same canonical Passkey continuation surface is reused for primary Passkey and password-bound Passkey MFA; the active MFA challenge determines which server orchestration is used.
The MFA begin/complete/token endpoints delegate challenge-bound proof to IPasskeyMfaAuthenticationService and establish browser or token session only after a proven AppUser is returned.

The Passkey MFA proof service validates provider=passkey, derives UserId from the password-issued challenge, invokes real user-bound WebAuthn proof, and consumes the MFA challenge only after successful proof.
Challenge validation enforces allowed-provider and durable-user binding; challenge consumption is single-use.
The real user-bound Passkey primitive validates WebAuthn challenge ownership, credential ownership, user verification, assertion proof, signature-counter advancement and step-up freshness.

Angular detects the retained MFA challenge, uses generated Passkey MFA begin/complete operations, clears the challenge only after successful completion, and otherwise retains the primary email-bound Passkey path.

React Native detects the in-memory MFA challenge, uses generated Passkey MFA begin/token completion, persists the returned AuthResponse, refreshes auth state, clears the MFA challenge after success, and otherwise retains the primary email-bound Passkey path.
Generated contracts expose createPasskeyMfaAuthenticationBegin, createPasskeyMfaAuthenticationComplete, and createPasskeyMfaAuthenticationToken.
Authored orchestration proof covers challenge binding, proof-before-consume ordering and rejection before Passkey proof for invalid MFA challenge.
Authored real-manager proof covers required user verification, challenge UserId binding, credential UserId binding, signature-counter advancement and MFA freshness.
When both TOTP and Passkey are enabled, either allowed provider may satisfy the same password-issued MFA challenge; devices unable to perform Passkey may complete with TOTP instead.
